case_descriptor: Lessons from §3.5.13 evidence and branch-only governance repair
summary: The completed chain separates §3.5.13 from adjacent prompt-injection, authority, monitoring and consequence categories and records a bounded Caelestis repair.
what_happened: The mechanism survived a full-inventory non-duplication test.
Caelestis implemented a direct control and named taxonomy subtype on its existing working branch.
governance_misconception: Treating the originating cyber incident, hostile input or resulting consequence as the failure mode obscures the independently repairable §3.5.13 mechanism.
integrated_learning: Classify the structural trust or assurance transition independently from threat capability and incident consequence.
Preserve provenance, authority boundaries and end-to-end assurance at the point where the mechanism arises.
Record branch-only governance repair without claiming canonical or external resolution.
risk_if_not_integrated: Evidence will be routed into broad catch-all records and the actual control boundary may remain unrepaired.
Local mitigations may suppress one exploit implementation while leaving the structural mechanism intact.
generalisation_boundary: The lesson does not establish malicious deployment, ecosystem prevalence, canonical Caelestis adoption or external-system conformance; ordinary prompt injection and threat capability alone remain outside this mechanism.
